questions.question: Name the four core industrial regions and explain why Gauteng dominates despite having no port and limited water.
questions.expected_answer: Gauteng (PWV), Durban–Pinetown, Port Elizabeth–Uitenhage and the South-Western Cape. Gauteng dominates because Witwatersrand gold drew capital, labour, railways and coal-fired power to the plateau; water was engineered in via the Vaal Dam and Lesotho Highlands scheme; and agglomeration then took over — skills, the country's richest market, converging transport and thousands of linked firms keep the region dominant even as gold fades. Industrial regions outlive their reasons.

questions.question: Outline the Port Elizabeth–Uitenhage region's location factors, main activities and chief weakness.
questions.expected_answer: Location: natural harbour on Algoa Bay, rail links inland, wool hinterland, and decisive investment by global vehicle makers, later reinforced by the deep-water port at Ngqura. Activities: vehicle assembly (Volkswagen at Kariega, Isuzu), a components belt including catalytic converters, tyres, food processing and port logistics. Chief weakness: dependence on a single industry — downturns in global car demand shake the whole region — compounded by water insecurity, load-shedding and provincial poverty.

questions.question: Distinguish SDIs from IDZs, give the flagship example of each, and state the balanced verdict on their success.
questions.expected_answer: An SDI is a corridor policy — government and private investment upgrade a whole route so economic activity develops along it; flagship: the Maputo Development Corridor from Gauteng to Maputo's port. An IDZ (now within the SEZ framework) is a point policy — a serviced industrial estate at a port or airport with incentives and duty-free inputs for export manufacturing; flagship: Coega beside Ngqura, with East London, Richards Bay, Dube TradePort and Saldanha as other examples. Verdict: real factories, jobs and freight have materialised, but at high cost per job and without breaking the four-region concentration — redistribution at the margin, not a redrawn map.
